League First Team (2023) }} {{nihongo|'''Yuki Kawamura'''|河村 勇輝|Kawamura Yūki}} (born 2 May 2001) is a Japanese professional [[basketball]] player who plays for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He previously played for the [[Chicago Bulls]] and [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. Kawamura also plays for the [[Japan men's national basketball team|Japan national team]], with whom he played at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2023 World Cup]] and [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]]. At {{cvt|5|ft|7|in}} tall, Kawamura was the shortest player during the [[2025–26 NBA season]]. ==Early life, family and high school== {{expand-section | date = August 2026}} Kawamura was born in [[Yanai, Yamaguchi]].{{cite web |last= Lohani |first= Suruchi |title= With unwavering support from his parents, Yuki Kawamura rises to become one of the NBA's renowned players |url=https://superstarbasketball.org/yuki-kawamura-parents-nba-memphis-grizzlies/ |website= SuperstarBasketball.com | publisher= Superstar Basketball |date= 2024-11-12| url-status= dead| archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20250428011651/https://superstarbasketball.org/yuki-kawamura-parents-nba-memphis-grizzlies/ | archivedate= 2025-04-28| accessdate= 2026-08-11}} His parents were very supportive of his basketball aspirations. Kawamura idolized professional and national team player [[Yuki Togashi]], who excelled despite being relatively short, at {{Height|m=1.68}}.{{cite web|title= Yuki Kawamura: Japan's next great XS-sized guard from Yuki Togashi|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/yuki-kawamura-japans-next-great-xs-sized-guard-from-yuki-togashi|website=FIBA.basketball|date=25 July 2024|access-date=8 August 2024}} Kawamura attended [[Fukuoka Daiichi High School]] and led its basketball team to back-to-back All-Japanese High School championships.{{cite web|title=How is high-school star Yuki Kawamura playing in Japan's professional B.League?|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/how-is-high-school-star-yuki-kawamura-playing-in-japan-s-professional-b-league|website= FIBA.basketball|date=27 January 2020|access-date=8 August 2024}} ==Professional career== ===San-en NeoPhoenix (2020)=== As a high schooler, Kawamura started his career under {{ill|special designated player|ja|特別指定選手}} status with the [[San-en NeoPhoenix]] in January 2020. In his first game, Kawamura became the youngest player in [[B.League]] history, at 18 years of age.{{cite web|first=Mikio|last=Irie|title=河村勇輝がB1デビュー戦で存在感を発揮。富樫勇樹はチーム掌握力に舌を巻いた|url=https://basketballking.jp/news/japan/b1/20200126/213042.html|work=バスケットボールキング|date=26 January 2020|access-date=10 September 2023|language=ja|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409221148/https://basketballking.jp/news/japan/b1/20200126/213042.html|archive-date=9 April 2023|url-status=live}} He later also became the youngest player to score in a B.League game. ===Yokohama B-Corsairs (2020–2024)=== During the offseason, Kawamura moved to Yokohama to join the [[Yokohama B-Corsairs]], still under special designation. Enrolling at [[Tokai University]],{{cite web |date=March 24, 2022 |title=Pro-bound Yuki Kawamura has a lofty goal on his mind with Akatsuki Five |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/pro-bound-yuki-kawamura-has-a-lofty-goal-on-his-mind-with-akatsuki-five |access-date=8 August 2024 |website=FIBA.basketball}} he left school to go pro at the beginning of the 2022–23 season. He immediately made an impact, winning the B.League's MVP award. In addition, with the B-Corsairs, he won Rookie of the Year and made the Best Five team.{{cite web|title=の表彰結果 ～横浜ビー・コルセアーズ 河村勇輝選手がB.LEAGUE史上初・MVPと新人賞をダブル受賞！～|trans-title=B.League Award Show 2022-23 ===Memphis Grizzlies / Hustle (2024–2025)=== {{Multiple image |align = left | perrow = 1 | total_width = 290 | image1 = | footer = }} On 6 September 2024, Kawamura signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]]{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Armando Bacot, Yuki Kawamura, Miye Oni, and Maozinha Pereira|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-armando-bacot-yuki-kawamura-miye-oni-and-maozinha-pereira|website=NBA.com|date=6 September 2024|access-date=6 September 2024}} and on 19 October, his training camp deal was converted into a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web |title=Grizzlies promote Yuki Kawamura to two-way contract |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-promote-yuki-kawamura-to-two-way-contract |website=Memphis Grizzlies |publisher=NBA}} On 14 October 2024, Kawamura scored a career-high 10 [[Basketball scorekeeping#Scoring|points]] and passed for seven [[assist (basketball)|assists]] in a 120–116 win against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |title=Edey shines in victory |url=https://www.nba.com/game/mem-vs-ind-0012400045/box-score |website=NBA |publisher=NBA.com}} ===Chicago Bulls / Windy City Bulls (2026)=== Kawamura joined the [[Chicago Bulls]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]]. On 19 July 2025, Kawamura signed a two-way contract with the Bulls.{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Yuki Kawamura to Two-Way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-yuki-kawamura-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2024|access-date=July 20, 2024}} He was released by the Bulls during training camp on 17 October, due to a lower right leg injury he sustained, which was later revealed to be a [[thrombus|blood clot]].{{cite web |last = Lorenzi |first = Joel |date = October 17, 2025 |title = Bulls waive Yuki Kawamura amid medical condition |website = [[The New York Times]] |url = https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6727185/2025/10/17/yuki-kawamura-bulls-status-injury-waived/ |access-date = 2026|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]}} ===Indiana Pacers (2026)=== On June 30, 2026, it was announced that Kawamura would be participating with the [[Indiana Pacers]] for the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |title=Pacers Announce 2026 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-announce-2026-summer-league-roster |website=[[NBA.com]] |publisher=[[Indiana Pacers]] |date=June 30, 2026 |access-date=July 1, 2026 }} ==National team career== Kawamura played for the [[Japan men's national under-13basketball team|Japan men's national under-16 team]] at the [[2017 FIBA Under-16 Asian Championship|2017 FIBA U16 Asian Championships]]. In six games, Kawamura averaged 5.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 4.3 assists.{{cite web |title=Yuki Kawamura in the FIBA U16 Asia Cup |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/228-fiba-u16-asia-cup/208017/players/249570-yuki-kawamura |website=FIBA Basketball |publisher=FIBA}} Kawamura made his [[Japan men's national basketball team]] debut in the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|2023 World Cup qualifiers]] against [[Chinese Taipei men's national basketball team|Taiwan]].{{cite web |title=Yuki Kawamura |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/249570-yuki-kawamura |website=FIBA Basketball |publisher=FIBA}} In a 89–49 victory, Kawamura recorded zero points, three rebounds, eight assists and five steals.{{cite web |title=1st Round |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/200-fiba-basketball-world-cup-qualifiers/208423/games/109215-JPN-TPE#boxscore |website=FIBA Basketball |publisher=FIBA}} Kawamura played six more qualifier games for Japan and averaged 10.4 points, 2.3 rebounds, 5.6 assists, and 2.7 steals.{{cite web |title=Yuki Kawarmura in the FIBA Basketball World Cup Qualifiers |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/200-fiba-basketball-world-cup-qualifiers/208423/players/249570-yuki-kawamura |website=FIBA Basketball |publisher=FIBA}} Kawamura represented Japan at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web |title=Hachimura, Watanabe and Kawamura top 25-man list of Japan candidates for World Cup |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/basketballworldcup-2023-news-hachimura-watanabe-and-kawamura-top-25-man-list-of-japan-candidates-for-world-cup |website=FIBA Basketball |publisher=FIBA}} Kawamura was an important contributor in Japan's 98–88 upset victory over [[Finland national basketball team|Finland]], as he accumulated 25 points, nine assists, and one rebound in Japan's first victory over a European team.{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=McNicol|title=Japan in tears after first ever win against European team in FIBA World Cup|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/08/27/sport/japan-fiba-basketball-world-cup-intl-hnk-spt/index.html|website=CNN.com|access-date=10 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829203619/https://www.cnn.com/2023/08/27/sport/japan-fiba-basketball-world-cup-intl-hnk-spt/index.html|archive-date=29 August 2023|url-status=live}}{{cite web |title=Japan vs. Finland |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/201-fiba-basketball-world-cup/208182/games/100746-JPN-FIN#boxscore |website=FIBA |publisher=FIBA Basketball}} In all five games, Kawamura averaged 13.6 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 7.6 assists.{{cite web |title=Yuki Kawamura at the FIBA Basketball World Cup |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/201-fiba-basketball-world-cup/208182/players/249570-yuki-kawamura |website=FIBA Basketball |publisher=FIBA}} The following year, Kawamura represented Japan at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]]. In the second game, they narrowly lost to [[France men's national basketball team|France]] 94–90 in overtime, and Kawamura scored a career-high 29 points, with seven rebounds and six assists in the effort.{{cite web|title=Kawamura: Meet the man who almost stunned host France|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/kawamura-willed-himself-into-olympics-spotlight-for-japan|website=FIBA.basketball|date=30 July 2024|access-date=8 August 2024}} In three games played, Kawamura averaged 20.3 points, 7.7 assists, and 3.3 rebounds.{{cite web |title=Yuki Kawamura |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/teams/japan/249570-yuki-kawamura |website=Paris 2024 |publisher=FIBA}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
